items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: And Dutre and Joe and Johnny and Baby, in fact the whole band except Lil, would meet there and we'd ask different questions.

ctx.x: So when was the first music that you were interested in? Did you start on the trombone or which instrument did you start on?

Well, my first instrument was trombone, but it wasn't my favorite instrument. I'd like to tell you, Bill, about how I come to study the trombone. While talking with Joe Oliver, it must have been somewhere around 1920, 1921, somewhere along there. He, I told Joe Oliver that I was going to take lessons on the trombone. So he says, why don't you try the clarinet? The reason Joe suggested to me to take the, take up the clarinet was because I used to whistle so good. And he said people did. So he thought if a fella…

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: How did you make out in the 50s with Natty Dominic and Baby and those guys?

ctx.x: And I used to sell Christmas trees. See, I'd sell somewhere around two or three thousand Christmas trees. And when everybody else was busted on Christmas day, I'm sitting there with eight or nine hundred dollars. See? I'd go out there, a lot of times I'd look and go out there in the freight yards. Sometimes a guy had a whole boxcar of Christmas trees. He's cold, you know? And they'd go in kind of slow and something like that. I bought a whole truck of trees and give a guy fifteen dollars. He wanted me to take…
How did you make out in the 50s with Natty Dominic and Baby and those guys?

I did all right. Dominic was another guy. He couldn't see me to begin with. I don't blame the guys. He told, I understand a little Creole or a little French. My people spoke it very well, but I never did pay much attention to it. But I understood what he was saying. He told Al and Omar Simien, what you got this guy for? He can't play. That's what he told him, see. Just like Johnny Dots. But he had to eat it up too. Because I just kept on trying. And after a while I began to bloom out. And then he began to hire me…
